claim: For the standard \(n\)-state Černý automaton \(C_n\), let \(\lambda_n(s)\) be the minimum length of a word whose image has size at most \(n-s\). For every \(n\ge 3\) and \(1\le s\le \lceil n/2ceil\), one has \(\lambda_n(s)=3s-2\).

correctness.rationale: Only the simple singular letter \(b\) can reduce image size, by at most one. After an effective \(b\), fewer than two intervening cycle letters \(a\) cannot make a later \(b\) effective, yielding length at least \(3s-2\). The witness \(b(a^2b)^{s-1}\) has an explicit missing-set induction and attains the bound for \(s\le\lceil n/2\rceil\). The included exact BFS independently confirms 40 finite parameter pairs.

evidence: Pin 1978 proves the square prescribed-rank bound for circular automata in the high-rank regime, which is an upper bound and does not give this exact value.
Rystsov 2025 proves the rank conjecture for Černý-type monoids, where rank threshold concerns maps of minimal monoid rank rather than all intermediate ranks.
broader_coverage.reasoning: These stronger-sounding general results do not imply equality for the intermediate deficiency threshold of the specific classical family.

value.rationale: The shortest length required to attain a prescribed deficiency is a natural synchronization invariant, and the Černý automata are the canonical extremal family. Determining the exact first-half profile gives a structural complement to the known worst-target avoidance threshold and separates early linear rank collapse from the eventual quadratic reset cost.
